title: Midyear priority alignment — field notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes to synthesize leadership input, early OKR drafts, and the proposed all-team orientation for the midyear planning window. This is intentionally lightweight — capture decisions we need to make in the next 10 days and the open risks to signal to execs before the town session.

Context & constraints:
- Timebox: 2-week planning runway before company-wide sync (tentative week of Nov 17).
- Audience: execs, eng leads, product, customer success, and finance.
- Primary question: which 3 company priorities do we carry into Q1 planning vs. which get deprioritized/tilted?
- Budget signal: finance needs high-level capacity ask by Nov 14 (headcount delta + infra burn estimate).

High-level thesis (draft):
- Focus on reliability & predictable unit economics: invest to reduce hosted per-token cost by 20% while hitting latency SLO targets for top 5 customer flows.
- Finish private deployment baseline (MVP) and two enterprise pilots to unlock pipeline this quarter.
- Developer experience: reduce onboarding time for internal SDKs and sample apps by 30% to lower friction for momentum.

Company-level OKR draft (starter, for iteration):
Objective A: Reduce inference unit cost and variance so customers can predict economics.
- KR A1: Achieve 20% reduction in median cost-per-1k-tokens on hosted API for production workloads (baseline: Sept cohort).
- KR A2: KV/pre-token cache hit rate >= 40% across top-10 hosted customers for interactive chat flows.
- KR A3: Deploy two optimized quantization profiles and validate latency/quality regression < 1% on eval harness.

Objective B: Deliver Private (VPC/on-prem) as enterprise-ready offering for regulated customers.
- KR B1: 2 running customer pilots in Private with completed SOC-ready attestations checklist.
- KR B2: Private deployment automation reduces time-to-standup from 6 weeks -> 2 weeks for blueprint config.
- KR B3: Signed purchase intent from >= 1 top-30 enterprise customer (legal term sheet).

Objective C: Improve platform reliability and operational transparency.
- KR C1: Reduce P99 tail latency for small-mesh chat (<= 350ms) in dedicated pools.
- KR C2: 99.95% uptime SLA for Dedicated across committed regions (month-long rolling window).
- KR C3: Instrument cost/latency per-request breadcrumbs in console for top 20 routes.

Notes on scope and tone:
- These are intentionally engineering-forward metrics (cost, latency, pilot completions). We should add a product engagement KR (NPS or activation) once we reconcile with Growth/CS.
- Consider replacing strict % cost target with a dollars-per-1M-token metric if finance prefers.

All-hands / midyear sync run-of-show (working):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome from CEO: one-sentence big decision (what we’re aligning on).
- 0:05–0:12 — State of the product: top-line metrics (latency, cost, pilots) — PM lead.
- 0:12–0:20 — OKR framing and trade-offs: Head of Product + Head of Eng.
- 0:20–0:30 — Customer vignette + enterprise pilot ask: Solutions Eng + CS.
- 0:30–0:40 — Breakout instructions + facilitated prioritization (live Miro).
- 0:40–0:55 — Breakouts (functional leads): pick 1 area to commit a scoped deliverable.
- 0:55–1:00 — Readouts & final ask (execs confirm 3 priorities).

Prep checklist (owners in parens):
- Compile top-10 hosted flows and baseline cost per flow (infra analytics) — (Ran/infra).
- Private pilot status notes + short risks doc — (Solutions Eng).
- Two one-slide asks for finance (headcount delta + infra cap) — (Head of Finance).
- Breakout canvases pre-seeded in Miro (3 lanes: Reliability, Private, Developer DX) — (People Ops + Product Ops).
- Communication: short preread + 6-min exec video to share 24h before — (CEO comms + DE).

Exec update talking points (for senior execs to use in pre-reads):
- Why this matters: customers buying inference care first about predictable costs and uptime; losing deals due to integration cadence and on-prem timelines.
- Hypothesis: a small, focused set of investments (autoscale logic, cache priming, 2 quant profiles, Private blueprint automation) unlocks >1.5x improvement in win rate for regulated deals.
- The ask: confirm the three priorities and the resource envelope for FY-end surge (engineering + Solutions Eng).

Risks we need to call out now:
- Risk: quantization regressions that pass our numeric eval but degrade customer-perceived quality. Mitigation: gated A/B with human evals + rollback path.
- Risk: Private pilot infra surprises (network, licensing) that extend timelines. Mitigation: early infra smoke tests with partner infra team.
- Risk: Headcount delays; hiring cadence can push pilot timelines. Mitigation: shift deliverable to automation and partner enablement.

Decision roll forward (how we’ll lock priorities after the org sync):
- Within 48 hours: consolidating breakouts into 1-page commitment by each function.
- By EOW: leadership to vote (email thread) to confirm 3 company priorities.
- By Nov 14: finance to provide budget gating decision based on asks.

Open questions / discussion items (quick):
- Do we want cost KR to be absolute (dollars) vs relative (%)? Who owns the metric synthesis (eng infra + finance)?
- Which customer flows count as "top-10"? Top by revenue or latency cost? Proposed: revenue-weighted active flows.
- Should we include a separate KR for developer onboarding time (DE metric) or bake into Objective C?

Appendix: supporting artifacts to attach to final doc
- Baseline infra cost table (sheet link) — TODO Ran to attach.
- Private pilot checklist (Confluence) — noted above.
- Eval harness summary + quality gate thresholds (Research) — Marcus to attach.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Ran: assemble flow-level cost baseline and one-slide summary (due Nov 10).
- Marcus: attach eval harness short doc and propose human-eval plan (due Nov 11).
- Lena: make breakout Miro frames and seed prompts + 3 example commitments (due Nov 12).
- Diego: draft finance ask slides and run with CFO for alignment (due Nov 13).
- Aisha: consolidate this doc into the preread and circulate (due Nov 12).

Notes to self / raw thinking (explicitly rough):
- We may need to phrase the private ask as "security & compliance enablement" to avoid the perception of shifting too many infra dollars at once.
- Breakouts should be constrained — ask teams to pick one "deliverable we can finish in 6 weeks" rather than vague ambitions.
- Consider a post-sync 6-week cadence check (30-min) for commitments: public readout of progress and slippage.

Unresolved small-buts-important items:
- Exact length of preread: 2 pages max + 6-min CEO video? (lean short).
- Mechanism for exec vote (Slack emoji vs Google Form) — prefer Form for auditability.

If you have comments, add inline or drop in slack #planning-week. This will be the source-of-truth draft until Nov 12 when I finalize the preread.

-- Aisha
